main.title: Marvel’s Spider-Man
main.subtitle: An experienced Spider-Man in New York
main.summary: Insomniac?s Marvel?s Spider-Man follows Peter Parker after eight years of fighting crime, with web-swinging, gadgets and acrobatic combat across New York.

cards.heading: Peter Parker after eight years
cards.text: Marvel?s Spider-Man is Insomniac Games? 2018 action adventure, published by Sony Interactive Entertainment for PlayStation 4. Peter Parker has already spent eight years fighting crime. Players swing across New York, tackle street crimes and use gadgets and acrobatics in combat, while Peter tries to balance his relationships and responsibilities.

cards.heading: Swinging between buildings
cards.text: Web lines attach to suitable points on buildings and trees. Animation, camera movement and field of view help preserve momentum, while wall running, point launches and web zips provide alternatives when there is no convenient swing point. Building height and spacing influence the routes players take.

cards.heading: Loading the city at speed
cards.text: To keep pace with Spider-Man, Insomniac divided the city into roughly eight hundred square tiles measuring 128 metres across. The game loads areas ahead of him and frees those left behind. This streaming system keeps the journey continuous as he crosses Manhattan.

cards.heading: Acrobatic combat and gadgets
cards.text: Spider-Man dodges, launches enemies into the air and uses webs to pin them to surfaces. Nearby objects and gadgets provide ways to separate a group or create space. Insomniac developed an acrobatic, improvised fighting style suited to an experienced hero.

cards.heading: Balancing Peter?s responsibilities
cards.text: Peter begins with years of experience using his powers and scientific knowledge. The story focuses on sustaining work, relationships and a secret identity alongside his role as Spider-Man. His competence in a fight does not make those responsibilities easier to balance.

cards.heading: Activities around the neighbourhood
cards.text: Street crimes, laboratories, collectibles and neighbourhood activities bring Spider-Man down between the buildings. Players interrupt longer journeys to respond to problems and explore particular streets, giving the city activities beyond the main missions.

cards.heading: The Advanced Suit
cards.text: Insomniac?s Advanced Suit places a large white spider on the chest, with white details on the gloves and boots. These contrasts help the limbs remain visible during fast movement against different backgrounds. The design gives this version of Peter a distinctive look while retaining Spider-Man?s familiar silhouette.

main.title: Astro Bot Rescue Mission
main.subtitle: A small robot in a world around the player
main.summary: Astro Bot Rescue Mission is Japan Studio's virtual-reality platform adventure, released for PlayStation VR on 2 October 2018.

cards.heading: A small robot in a world around the player
cards.text: Astro Bot Rescue Mission is Japan Studio's virtual-reality platform adventure, released for PlayStation VR on 2 October 2018. Captain Astro searches five worlds for his scattered robot crew, running and jumping under the player's control. The headset places the player inside the same space as the small hero, giving each platform and distant hiding place a physical scale. Finding a missing bot can mean looking around an obstacle or leaning towards a corner, making observation part of the journey alongside Astro's movement.

cards.heading: Look beyond the obvious path
cards.text: Twenty levels arrange the search around different settings, with bosses closing each world. Rescued crew members help unlock those encounters, giving exploration a purpose beyond reaching an exit. The player controls Astro with a DualShock 4 while also watching the surrounding environment independently. That separation lets the hero continue along a narrow route as attention shifts towards something beside or behind it. A platformer's familiar question of where to go gains another dimension: the place worth investigating may sit outside the direction Astro is facing.

cards.heading: The controller enters the rescue
cards.text: The player's own presence also affects the world, from head movements that break obstacles to breath detected by the headset's microphone. Gadgets associated with the controller add further interactions to the stages. Kenneth C. M. Young's music accompanies the robots' expressive animation and changing situations. Directed by Nicolas Doucet, the game grew from characters introduced in The Playroom projects. Its central achievement is the partnership between the small character being guided and the much larger observer whose attention and movements help make the rescue possible.

date_context_only.region: Standard edition worldwide release on Xbox One and Windows, October 2, 2018; Ultimate Edition early access began September 28.

main.title: Forza Horizon 4
main.summary: Forza Horizon 4 is a 2018 racing game developed by Playground Games and published by Microsoft Studios.

cards.heading: A festival on British roads
cards.text: Forza Horizon 4 is a 2018 racing game developed by Playground Games and published by Microsoft Studios. It was released on 2 October 2018 for Windows and Xbox One after being announced at Xbox's E3 2018 conference. An enhanced version was released on Xbox Series X/S on 10 November 2020.

cards.heading: A landscape changed by the seasons
cards.text: The game is set in a fictionalised representation of areas of Great Britain. It is the fourth Forza Horizon title, following Forza Horizon 3, and the eleventh  instalment  in the Forza series. The game is noted for its introduction of changing seasons to the series, as well as featuring several content-expanding updates which have included new game modes. A sequel, Forza Horizon 5, was released on 9 November 2021. Forza Horizon 4 was delisted from sale on 15 December 2024 across all platforms.

main.title: Mega Man 11
main.subtitle: Speed Gear and Power Gear
main.summary: Mega Man 11 adds the Double Gear System to the classic series? running, jumping and Robot Master weapons.

cards.heading: The classic series returns
cards.text: Mega Man 11 is Capcom?s 2018 side-scrolling action game, released in October for PlayStation 4, Switch, Xbox One and PC. The first numbered classic-series entry in eight years retains the Mega Buster and weapons earned from defeated Robot Masters. Its Double Gear System adds temporary control over speed and attack power.

cards.heading: Slowing the action with Speed Gear
cards.text: Speed Gear slows the action, giving the player more time to react to attacks and obstacles. Mega Man still needs to be positioned correctly and jumps must still be made. The system overheats with extended use, so players choose when to activate it and when to let it cool.

cards.heading: Weapons and Power Gear
cards.text: Defeating a Robot Master awards a weapon with its own behaviour and trajectory. Different weapons suit different enemies and situations. Power Gear temporarily strengthens those tools, adding a choice between ordinary attacks and a stronger burst of force.

cards.heading: A 3D look for side-on movement
cards.text: Characters and scenery are rendered in 3D while movement remains side-on. Platforms, enemies and jump distances retain the basic structure of the earlier games. The new presentation updates their appearance while keeping these obstacles easy to identify.

main.title: Super Mario Party
main.subtitle: Separate paths return to the party
main.summary: Super Mario Party is NDcube's first Switch entry, released on 5 October 2018.

cards.heading: Separate paths return to the party
cards.text: Super Mario Party is NDcube's first Switch entry, released on 5 October 2018. Players again travel independently around boards, collecting coins and purchasing Stars while minigames interrupt each round. A single Joy-Con provides each person's controls, allowing motion sensing and HD Rumble to shape the short activities. The return to separate routes restores a familiar kind of rivalry: the next turn concerns the player's own position, the nearest prize and what the other characters might do before that destination can be reached.

cards.heading: A character’s own dice change the plan
cards.text: Each character brings an alternative dice block with a particular set of outcomes. Choosing between it and the standard die makes movement partly a question of risk, with some characters favoring reliable numbers and others offering a larger reward alongside a possible loss. Recruited allies contribute additional rolls and lend their own dice. A useful partnership therefore changes the options available on a later turn, giving character selection and recruitment a practical role in planning a route around the board.

cards.heading: Cooperate beyond the race for Stars
cards.text: Eighty minigames provide different mixtures of individual competition, teams and motion control. Other modes place cooperation more centrally, extending the gathering beyond a single race for Stars. The score was composed by Masayoshi Ishi, Toshiki Aida, Satoshi Okubo and Naruki Kadosaka. Super Mario Party combines a return to the older board structure with ideas drawn from Switch's small, shareable controllers. Its changes are most visible in the hands of the group: each participant has a personal dice choice, but another ally or a cooperative challenge can change the relationship for a moment.

date_context_only.region: Original standard release on PlayStation 4, Xbox One and Windows, October 5, 2018.

main.title: Assassin's Creed Odyssey
main.subtitle: A mercenary?s journey through ancient Greece
main.summary: An adventure through fifth-century BCE Greece with dialogue choices, naval travel and role-playing progression.

cards.heading: Choices and naval travel in ancient Greece
cards.text: Developed mainly by Ubisoft Qu?bec, Assassin?s Creed Odyssey takes the series to fifth-century BCE Greece. Players choose Kassandra or Alexios and follow a family story through dialogue choices, role-playing progression and naval travel. Mountains, cities and islands provide settings for assignments and exploration.

cards.heading: Kassandra or Alexios
cards.text: The chosen mercenary meets people from different communities and decides how to respond. Dialogue can express openness, threats, humour or distance, affecting relationships and the course of encounters. The family story connects these journeys across the wider map.

cards.heading: Sailing aboard the Adrestia
cards.text: The Adrestia carries the protagonist between islands. Sailing lets players approach new coasts, recruit crew members and take part in naval battles. The ship remains a familiar base as the surrounding regions change.

cards.heading: History and Greek mythology
cards.text: Political conflict and daily life share the setting with legendary creatures, including Medusa. The game combines its reconstruction of ancient Greece with mythology and the series? own science-fiction framework. These encounters add different opponents and locations to the adventure.

main.title: RimWorld
main.subtitle: A colony with a history
main.summary: RimWorld is Ludeon Studios' science-fiction colony simulation, released as version 1.0 in October 2018 after a long public-development period. Survivors arrive on a distant planet and must build shelter, obtain food and establish a settlement. The inhabitants bring skills, relationships and personal needs into that work. The chosen AI storyteller organises events around them, producing raids, visitors and other disruptions. Construction and resource management provide the setting for stories that emerge from what individual people experience and how the colony responds.

cards.heading: A colony with a history
cards.text: RimWorld is Ludeon Studios' science-fiction colony simulation, released as version 1.0 in October 2018 after a long public-development period. Survivors arrive on a distant planet and must build shelter, obtain food and establish a settlement. The inhabitants bring skills, relationships and personal needs into that work. The chosen AI storyteller organises events around them, producing raids, visitors and other disruptions. Construction and resource management provide the setting for stories that emerge from what individual people experience and how the colony responds.

cards.heading: People before efficiency
cards.text: A colonist's abilities affect the work they can perform, while injuries, fatigue and mood change how reliably they do it. A good researcher may be poorly suited to negotiations; a wounded leg can slow someone needed for an urgent task. Bedrooms, meals and relationships influence daily life alongside workshops and stores. Improving production therefore involves more than arranging efficient buildings. The people carrying out the plan need treatment, rest and suitable conditions, and disagreements can make an otherwise orderly settlement difficult to manage.

cards.heading: Events that change the plan
cards.text: The environment gives each settlement different pressures. A cold region limits the growing season, while other locations bring heat, disease or different resources. Preparing food and shelter creates room to respond when a fire, animal attack or raid interrupts normal work. Caravans allow trade, journeys and contact with other factions beyond the home map. The storyteller's events connect these systems: losing supplies can change a medical decision, which may alter a colonist's relationships and the next problem the group must solve.

main.title: Return of the Obra Dinn
main.summary: Return of the Obra Dinn is a 2018 adventure and puzzle video game created by Lucas Pope and published by 3909 LLC.

cards.heading: Lucas Pope?s second commercial game
cards.text: Return of the Obra Dinn is a 2018 adventure and puzzle video game created by Lucas Pope and published by 3909 LLC. It was Pope's second commercial game, following 2013's Papers, Please, and was first released for macOS and Windows before being ported to Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One a year later. Return of the Obra Dinn was praised for its gameplay, art style, and narrative; it won several awards, including the Seumas McNally Grand Prize.

cards.heading: Investigating the fate of sixty people
cards.text: The game is set in 1807 with the player assuming the role of an unnamed investigator for the East India Company. The Obra Dinn, a merchant ship missing for five years, has reappeared off the coast of England with no known surviving crew or passengers. The player is dispatched to the ghost ship to perform an appraisal, reconstruct the events of the voyage, and determine the fates of all sixty souls aboard, providing a cause of death for those deceased or a probable current location for those presumed living. Investigation is accomplished through the use of the "Memento Mortem", a pocket watch capable of recreating a death at the moment it occurred. The game, played in first-person perspective, uses a "1-bit" monochromatic graphical style inspired by games on early Macintosh computers.

cards.heading: Recognition for its puzzles and visual style
cards.text: Return of Obra Dinn first released on macOS and Windows on October 18, 2018. It received generally positive reviews from critics who praised its story, puzzles, creativity, and favorably compared it to Her Story (2015). It was cited by several outlets as among the best video games of 2018, and retrospectively, one of the greatest of all time.

main.title: Red Dead Redemption 2
main.subtitle: Arthur Morgan and the Van der Linde gang
main.summary: Red Dead Redemption 2 follows Arthur Morgan and the Van der Linde gang through the final years of the outlaw era.

cards.heading: Arthur Morgan and the gang
cards.text: Red Dead Redemption 2 is Rockstar?s 2018 Western adventure for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One. Set before the first game, it follows Arthur Morgan and the Van der Linde gang. Camps, horses, wildlife and contextual conversations accompany missions across a changing frontier. The PC version followed in November 2019.

cards.heading: Life around the camp
cards.text: The gang?s members eat, argue, sing and react to recent events at camp. Arthur can bring supplies, perform tasks or spend time listening to conversations. Returning between missions reveals relationships and tensions that change with the group?s fortunes.

cards.heading: Greeting or antagonising strangers
cards.text: Arthur can greet, antagonise or respond to people he meets. Available options depend on the situation and earlier behaviour. A hostile exchange can escalate, while a calmer response changes how an encounter develops.

cards.heading: Travelling with a horse
cards.text: Horses have different speeds and gaits, respond to slopes and obstacles, and grow more closely bonded to Arthur through care and repeated use. Rockstar synchronised horse and rider animations to make movement work across varied terrain. Choosing a route also means considering how the animal can cross it.

cards.heading: Placing shots with Dead Eye
cards.text: Dead Eye slows the action so Arthur can identify targets and mark shots. Its capabilities expand through several levels of use. The player still needs to manage the ability?s resources and choose a position before normal speed resumes.

cards.heading: A score that follows the action
cards.text: Woody Jackson?s score combines narrative, ambient and interactive components. Some music accompanies specific missions, while other layers change as Arthur rides, explores or causes trouble. More than one hundred musicians contributed to the score and its sounds.

cards.heading: Reactions across the frontier
cards.text: Witnesses, law enforcement, wildlife and routines respond to the player?s actions. A small incident can draw in other people and the authorities, creating consequences outside a planned mission. Contextual animation helps show reactions such as a witness fleeing or a horse avoiding an obstacle.

main.title: Déraciné
main.subtitle: An unseen visitor in frozen time
main.summary: Déraciné is FromSoftware's virtual-reality adventure, released for PlayStation VR on 6 November 2018.

cards.heading: An unseen visitor in frozen time
cards.text: Déraciné is FromSoftware's virtual-reality adventure, released for PlayStation VR on 6 November 2018. The player becomes an unseen faerie in a secluded boarding school, exploring a world suspended in time. Children and objects provide fragments of a mystery that develops as the visitor finds ways to affect their lives. The quiet setting asks for close attention rather than speed: a small alteration to something in the room can become evidence that the invisible being exists and is trying to communicate.

cards.heading: Small changes establish a presence
cards.text: Moving through frozen moments lets the player examine the school and gather information from details that ordinary time would carry past. Objects become a means of reaching the children, who gradually recognize the faerie's presence. The story later shifts through time, making previous discoveries part of understanding another moment. Its central relationship grows through those indirect exchanges. The player occupies the same rooms as the inhabitants while remaining separate from them, a distance that turns observation and intervention into the adventure's principal actions.

cards.heading: A mystery assembled from quiet moments
cards.text: Hidetaka Miyazaki and FromSoftware collaborated with Japan Studio on the project, using PlayStation VR and two Move controllers to revisit the measured pace of a traditional adventure. Fragmented storytelling connects the school's mysteries to the bond with its children. Music by Tsukasa Saitoh, Shoi Miyazawa and Yuka Kitamura supports that restrained atmosphere. The headset gives the quiet spaces a physical presence, while the frozen-time premise explains the player's unusual place within them: close enough to notice and change things, but unable simply to join the ordinary flow of life.
